question: In the InfoGripe bulletin for epidemiological week 44 of 2026 (expected 12 November 2026), what will Brazil's national long-term SRAG trend be reported as?

calls.reasoning: Status quo at SE42: long-term stability/oscillation, short-term growth, slight COVID-19 rise, 5 states at alert with growth. 2026 SE35-42 long-term signals: stability x4, decline x3, growth x0. Late-season 2025 (SE46-47) was decline. Persistent short-term growth through SE43-44 could flip the long-term window (SE39-44) to growth, but earlier short-term growth signals (SE38-39) did not translate into long-term growth. SE43 summary was not yet published (404) at time of research. No human market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers.

calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts. The only factual discrepancy was the stability count over SE35-42 (Run 3 said 5); the background's list gives 4 stability and 3 decline across 7 editions, and either count leaves growth at 0. SE43 has not been published, so nothing settles the growth question directly. The judgment call: short-term growth plus the COVID-19 uptick and the rise in states with growth make a flip to growth over the SE39-44 window plausible, weighed against two earlier short-term growth spells that reverted. I take stability as modal and put growth slightly above the runs' typical figure because the late-season COVID-19 momentum compounds. No web access on this run.
